name: Lure of the Lurkerfish
text: The gently oscillating blue- green lights seen by the riverbank at dusk and dawn are sometimes mistaken for fireflies. Any Character passing a Hard (−2 SL) Lore (Riverways) Test will know that these are likely to be the lures of Lurkerfish. Those who fail the Lore Test must make an Easy (+4 SL) Cool Test or become beguiled by the sight and unable to perform any action except moving towards the light — effectively acquiring the Unconscious Condition.
adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty uses current SL modifiers.

name: Slimy
text: Latch-eels can produce a surprising quantity of slime, in or out of the water. If a Latch-eel is ever Grappled by an opponent, it may make a Toughness Test. If it succeeds, it produces a clump of slime, benefiting from +4 SL to subsequent Tests to break free. The opponent must make a Challenging (+0 SL) Athletics Test. Failure means that slime has covered their face, and the opponent must either release the Latch-eel or start to suffer suffocation (WFRP, page 181).

name: Love the Light
text: Daggerfish are attracted to light. Attempts to use fire to deter them only encourages them further. Whilst they possess the Bestial trait, they do not shy from fire or take Broken Conditions from being struck by flaming attacks.

name: Immersion
text: The Sea Elemental may attempt to immerse its opponents by making a Grapple. If the Sea Elemental inflicts an Entangled Condition on its opponent, it draws them into its own body. The immersed character suffers from Suffocation as detailed on WFRP, page 181. They may attempt to escape by freeing themselves from the Entangled Condition as if they were Grappled by the Sea Elemental, making Opposed Strength Tests against its Strength of 59 to break free. However, the Sea Elemental does not need to actively maintain the Grapple — it may act as if the immersed character were not there and does not count as being Engaged.

name: Fire Resistant
text: Sea Elementals never suffer from Ablaze Conditions.

name: Mindless Spellcaster
text: Sea Elementals may use their Strength Characteristic for the purpose of casting spells and channelling.

name: Boat Crusher
text: The Gargantuan may attempt to constrict a vessel of Size Large or smaller. To constrict a vessel, it must spend one turn wrapping itself about the vessel for every 10 points of Size the vessel possesses. Once the vessel is wrapped up, the Gargantuan starts to squeeze — making an Extended Opposed Strength Test against the boat’s Toughness. Once the SL reaches the boat’s Wounds, the boat shatters, reduced to a mass of flotsam. During this time, the boat’s crew may attack the Gargantuan or attempt to lever it from the boat. Attacks that inflict more than 7 Wounds may cause the Gargantuan to let go if it fails a subsequent Average (+2 SL) Cool Test. Levering the Gargantuan requires making an Opposed Strength Test against the creature. A result of 0 to 4 SL prevents it from squeezing the boat that turn, and a result of 5 SL or more forces it to release the boat.
adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty uses current SL modifiers.

name: Electrical Discharge
text: If the creature successfully Grapples an opponent, then at the start of its subsequent turns, the creature can spend 1 Momentum to deliver an electric shock to the Grappled character. The electrical discharge inflicts a hit of 10 Damage which ignores non- magical metal armour. Any Character taking Wounds from the electrical attack must also pass a Difficult (−1 SL) Endurance Test or suffer a Stunned Condition. The Gargantuan cannot make electrical attacks with impunity. Each time it uses the attack, it must make an Average (+2 SL) Endurance Test. Failure indicates that it suffers a Fatigued Condition. Whilst the Gargantuan is under the effects of a Fatigued Condition, electrical discharge attacks only inflict Damage 6 hits which ignore non-magical metal armour. The Gargantuan may also discharge electricity when it has Grappled a boat. This does no damage against the boat, but the crew all receive a jolt, suffering a Damage 6 hit (reduced to a Damage 3 hit if the Gargantuan has a Fatigued Condition).
adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty uses current SL modifiers. Printed Advantage uses Momentum.

name: Whale Bane
text: All Fanged Maw attacks have core Venom (Difficult −1 SL recovery): causing Wounds inflicts Poisoned; the Difficulty applies to recovery.
adaptation: Uses full Fifth Edition Venom rather than the older on-hit interpretation.

name: Syreen’s Call
text: As an action the Syreen may sing its luring song. Characters within a number of yards equal to the Syreen’s Initiative must make an Difficult (−1 SL) Cool Test or become beguiled by the call and unable to perform any action except moving towards the Syreen — effectively acquiring the Unconscious Condition.
adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty uses current SL modifiers.

name: Resistant to Cold
text: Any weapon, spell, or effect that inflicts damage or impairment due to cold will likely have a reduced impact on an Orb Leviathan. It may make an Endurance Test to ignore any ill effects from cold and ice.

name: Lure of the Leviathan
text: The first sign of an approaching attack by an Orb Leviathan is a lambent yellow light drifting slowly underwater. Any Character passing a Hard (−2 SL) Lore (Oceans) Test will have heard about the lure of the Orb Leviathan, and may look away before it takes effect. Those who fail the Lore Test must succeed on an Easy (+4 SL) Cool Test or acquire the Stunned Condition.
adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty uses current SL modifiers.

name: Devastating Assault
text: When a Black Leviathan charges a ship, it causes a collision with a CR of 50.

name: On a Different Scale
text: The Black Leiviathan possesses the Bestial Trait and can be scared by fire. However, guttering torches are too small to attract its notice, let alone scare it. To benefit from the frightening qualities of fire, the blaze must be the size and intensity of a large bonfire; anything less isn’t going to concern the Black Leviathan. When considering the psychological impact of other sources of Fear and Terror, the GM should consider that unless the source is something the Black Leviathan should respect in terms of size, it is unlikely to bother the beast. Unearthly as Daemonettes, Zombies, and wizards with flaming heads may be, the Black Leviathan regards them all as fish food.

name: Marine Creature
text: The creature is at home in the ocean and unsuited to life on land. Its printed profile assumes an aquatic environment and it moves its full Movement in water. Out of water, Movement drops to 1 and all its Tests suffer −2 SL. It must be regularly doused with water or begin to suffocate (core Suffocation).
